SwitchPreference.android:summary: Start the first word of a sentence with a capital letter

SwitchPreference.android:title: Period with double-space
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Type two spaces in a row to get a period and a space. The second space has to come within the Multipress threshold under Timing (750 ms by default), otherwise you just get two spaces.

Preference.android:title: Test the spell checker
Preference.android:summary: Asks the spell checker about a few misspelled words and shows what it answers and what auto-correct would do. Use it to find out why typos are not being fixed.

A misspelled word is fixed when you type a space or punctuation after it, or press Enter. The best guess is picked from the spell checker chosen in Android's Languages & input settings, the built in common words and the words you use, counting slips of the fingers (a key next to the right one, swapped or doubled letters) and how common each word is. Higher levels dare more. Slang like lol and omg, stretched words like sooo, and names are left alone. Press Backspace straight away to put it back, and it won't be fixed again. Corrections you choose or keep are remembered as habits. Fixing is off in Cyrillic and Korean, and in fields for passwords, addresses and the like.

Basic fixes what is always wrong: a lowercase i, a missing apostrophe (dont), a apple, could of, alot and a doubled the, capitals for the first word of a sentence and for days, months, languages and places, caps lock slips (hELLO), and takes the space away from before a comma, full stop, question mark or exclamation mark. Full also chooses between their, there and they're, your and you're, its and it's, to and too, then and than, lose and loose, whose and who's, and fixes he don't, they was, I have went and were going. It looks at the words you have typed, never at what comes after, so it only acts on patterns that are hardly ever right. Press Backspace straight away to undo a fix, and it won't be fixed again.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Space after punctuation
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Put in the space when a full stop, comma, question mark or exclamation mark is typed straight into the next word: hello.world becomes hello. world. Web addresses, file names and abbreviations are left alone.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Split words that ran together
SwitchPreference.android:summary: lovehahaha becomes love hahaha and goodmorning becomes good morning. Only for a word that is not a word itself and splits into common ones.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Fix the last word when I press Enter
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Fixes the word before the cursor just before Enter is sent, so the last word of a message is fixed too. When it changes something, Enter is sent again straight after the fix.

EditTextPreference.android:title: Shortcuts and my words
EditTextPreference.android:dialogMessage: One per line. A shortcut is replaced when you type a space after it: omw = on my way. A word on its own line is never fixed and is suggested as you type it: Kubernetes.
EditTextPreference.android:summary: Shortcuts that turn into longer text, and words that are never fixed

SwitchPreference.android:title: Show toolbar
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Show a strip above the keyboard with emoji, clipboard and voice buttons, word suggestions, and the active modifiers

SwitchPreference.android:title: Word suggestions and spell check
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Suggest corrections and completions in the toolbar. Corrections come from the spell checker chosen in Android's Languages & input settings. With Emoji held, F, G and H pick the first, second and third suggestion.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Complete with common English words
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Also suggest words from a built in list of 30,000 common English words, after the ones you use. Turn this off if you mostly type another language.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Learn words as I type
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Remember the words you use, which words follow which, how you start sentences, and the corrections you make, to suggest and fix things the way you write. It is only stored on this device, and never from password fields.

Preference.android:title: Manage learned words
Preference.android:summary: See what it has learned and forget the words or corrections you don't want. You can also hold a suggestion in the toolbar to forget it.

Preference.android:title: Import text to learn from
Preference.android:summary: Learn words and which words follow which from a text file (your notes, exported chats, or a book), so suggestions work right away. The file is only read on this device.

Preference.android:title: Clear learned words
Preference.android:summary: Forget every word that was learned from typing

Preference.app:summary: Assign actions for tap, long press, and hold + key combinations for certain keys.

SeekBarPreference.android:title: History size
SeekBarPreference.android:summary: The number of copied items to keep. Pinned items are always kept.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Skip sensitive items
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Don't keep what password managers and other apps mark as sensitive (Android 13 and later)

SwitchPreference.android:title: Show a map when I press Sym
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Press Sym and leave it for a moment, and a map of the keyboard appears with the additional characters of every key: hold a key for the first one and press it again for the next ones, and the accents in italics if they are turned on. It goes away when you press a key or let go of Sym.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Enable accented characters
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Press a vowel again straight away to put an accent on it: press e twice for é, three times for è. This is off until you want it. It takes over quick double letters like ee and oo, so words like meet and book get accents while it is on. The time allowed between presses is the Multipress threshold under Timing.

SwitchPreference.android:title: Only vowels
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Disable multipress for consonants (like ç or ß) and only accent vowels

SwitchPreference.android:title: Enable ligatures
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Type ae or oe and get the ligature æ or œ, as in the French œuvre

SwitchPreference.android:title: Enable Cyrillic Layer
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Long press right-shift to toggle Cyrillic layer

SwitchPreference.android:title: Enable Korean Input
SwitchPreference.android:summary: Long press right-shift to toggle Korean Input

Preference.android:summary: These decide how the keyboard reads a key press. All are in milliseconds (1000 ms is one second). Change them if a double tap locks Shift when you only meant a tap, or the other way round, or if the double-space period or holding a key for its symbol is unreliable.

SeekBarPreference.android:title: Multipress threshold (ms)
SeekBarPreference.android:summary: How soon after pressing a key a second press of the same key, or holding it down, still counts as part of it. It decides three things. Double-space for a period: the second Space must come within this time. Holding a key for its alternate character (hold a letter for the symbol Alt gives): the key has to start repeating within this time, and pressing it again within this time steps through the next alternate. It also applies to the long press of the Mic/Period and Emoji/0 keys. Lower means quicker taps are needed. Higher is more forgiving. Keep it well above the time your phone waits before a held key starts repeating (about half a second), or holding a key does nothing. Default 750.

SeekBarPreference.android:title: Modifier lock threshold (ms)
SeekBarPreference.android:summary: How close together two taps on Shift or Alt must be to lock it. Tap it twice within this time and it stays on until you press it again, like caps lock. For the Sym key it is the boundary between a tap and a hold: a press shorter than this latches Sym on until you press it again, and holding it longer makes it work only while it is held down. Lower means a faster double tap is needed. Higher is easier to lock but a second tap made just after the first can lock it by accident. Default 250.

SeekBarPreference.android:title: Modifier long press threshold (ms)
SeekBarPreference.android:summary: How long Shift or Alt can be held before it stops counting as a quick tap. Tap it (let go before this time) and it applies to the next key only, so tap Shift and then a letter to get one capital. Hold it longer than this and it works only while it is held down, and is dropped when you let go. Lower means a slower tap already counts as a hold. Higher gives you more time to tap, but a long, slow press can then arm the next key by accident. Default 350.
